summary: Request: Incremental SIEM webhook ACK manifest, replay tokens, and security questionnaire evidence for on‑boarding
description: Issue summary: Nordic Bank is onboarding Redwood audit exports via our webhook bridge. They require an incremental delivery manifest that proves at-least-once delivery with per-batch signed ACKs and replay tokens, plus security questionnaire evidence (SAML assertions, KMS/HSM attestation sample, and retention policy). Impact: They cannot complete security review for escrow and incident response automation without cryptographic delivery proofs and sample resume tokens. Environment: prod-us-east; customer uses an on-prem SIEM behind a corporate firewall with an ingestion webhook that validates signed manifests. Request: 1) Provide a sample signed ACK manifest format for incremental webhook batches (including timestamp, batch_id, resume_token, hmac signature, signer_cert_fingerprint). 2) Deliver a 48-hour sample bundle (NDJSON) with two consecutive batches showing resume tokens and signed ACKs. 3) Provide redacted SAML assertion examples and the audit-exporter key attestation statement for their compliance pack. 4) Answer security questionnaire sections 3.1 (key management) and 4.2 (replay/resume guarantees).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer configured inbound webhook with mutual TLS and expects per-batch ACK header 'X-Redwood-ACK' containing signed manifest. 2) Send two test payloads (batch A then batch B) via the platform with resume tokens generated. 3) Observe that customer received two payloads but their SIEM reported duplicated event IDs when webhook retried. 4) Confirm whether the platform provided resume_token rotation and manifest for each batch and whether ACK signature verification would have prevented duplicate acceptance. 5) Reproduce by replaying batch A with previous resume_token and check consumer acceptance behavior.
impact: Onboarding blocked for enterprise compliance review; inability to provide signed delivery evidence prevents SOC and IR teams from closing contractual controls. Potential risk to incident reconstruction if replay tokens are ambiguous. Customer reports small delta in event counts between our delivery logs and their SIEM (2-3 events per day) which they attribute to retries/duplicates.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (2025-02-12): Audit-exporter is emitting per-batch resume_token and a detached JWS manifest. Webhook-proxy logs show successful mtls and ACK header verification for the sample window. Customer-provided SIEM logs show duplicate event ids after a retry window; hypothesis: consumer side replay handling accepts replays when resume_token not advanced or when dedupe keys differ. Checked signing key rotation: rotation window aligned with our documented 24h rotation; no gap found. Noted a mismatch: customer's ingestion pipeline de-duplicates based on 'event_uuid' while our retry may reingest with the same event_uuid but different envelope_id; recommend mapping guidance. Security evidence: can produce a signed manifest (JWS) example using current audit-exporter key, and produce an HSM attestation excerpt from our HSM provider (redacted).

public_notes: We supplied a signed manifest format and short-term workaround. Root cause: customer dedupe logic did not include envelope_id leading to duplicate acceptance on retry. Recommended dedupe change and provided signed proofs for compliance. Pending final signed evidence bundle and legal appendix.
private_notes: Consider adding an explicit 'envelope_id' header to future webhook deliveries to make dedupe guidance clearer. Evaluate changing resume_token semantics to include monotonic counter in addition to opaque token. Track as potential small product enhancement under ops backlog.
